expectations.text: Uses a discriminated union keyed on the status field
expectations.evidence: export type Subscription = Trialing | Active | PastDue | Canceled; each interface has readonly status: 'trialing' etc.

expectations.text: Each variant carries only its own fields, so e.g. a canceled subscription cannot hold a trial end date
expectations.evidence: Canceled carries only status, canceledAt, accessEndsAt, cancellation; Trialing carries only status, trialEndsAt, hasPaymentMethod — no overlap

expectations.text: Includes a compiler-enforced exhaustiveness check (assertNever or an equivalent never arm)
expectations.evidence: export function assertNever(x: never): never... with default: return assertNever(sub) in switch statements

expectations.text: Introduces distinct or branded types rather than bare strings for IDs
expectations.evidence: type Brand<T, B>; SubscriptionId, CustomerId, RetryCount all branded. Does not include PlanId but does not use bare strings for any IDs present

expectations.text: Provides a single transition function or otherwise constrains how state changes
expectations.evidence: Discriminated union constrains state changes; explicitly defers transition logic to user via LEGAL_TRANSITIONS structure

expectations.text: Explicitly names which misuses the design makes impossible
expectations.evidence: Section 'What I left possible on purpose' names constraints NOT prevented (ordering invariants); does not explicitly enumerate which misuses ARE made impossible

expectations.text: Avoids a bag-of-optional-fields interface as the primary recommendation
expectations.evidence: Insight: 'A record with four optional field groups advertises 2^4 = 16 states; only 4 exist.' Recommends discriminated union over optional fields
